title: Runtime Telemetry Decoder for Per-Route/Model/Customer Cost & Latency Attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a decoding layer and pipeline that converts raw runtime traces and token telemetry into deterministic, auditable cost and latency attributions scoped to route, model variant, and customer. This ticket covers schema design, streaming+microbatch transformation, a fallback heuristic for missing KV/trace fragments, and a verification harness that compares decoder output to existing rollup metrics. Goal is to provide per-request and aggregated views with configurable temporal granularity (1s / 1m / 1h).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Decoder produces per-request attribution records that include: route_id, model_variant, customer_id, token_count, compute_ms, gpu_util_estimate, cache_hits, attribution_confidence.
2) Aggregates match existing billing rollups within +/- 2% for a full-day synthetic workload.
3) Latency SLO tags (p99, p90) are derivable from decoder output without additional joins.
4) Fallback heuristics detect missing KV-cache markers and mark records as low-confidence.
5) End-to-end pipeline runs in streaming mode with <5s tail latency for 95% of events and supports replay via microbatch.
6) Schema docs and open PR for runtime instrumentation merged, and basic dashboard widgets in Console pointing to decoder metrics are available.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: ingest runtime traces (kinesis/topic) -> lightweight enrich (route/model/customer lookups) -> streaming transform (Flink/Beam) that decodes per-token KV lineage + kernel selection metadata -> emit attribution events to econ-store (columnar) and a high-throughput hotpath for per-request detail.
Key decoders:
- KV-aware token mapper: reconstructs cache hit/miss sequences using sequence ids and optional KV markers injected at runtime.
- Kernel-cost estimator: uses model profile table (seq_len buckets) to convert kernel counts to ms and normalized GPU-seconds.
- Confidence scorer: outputs confidence tag (high/medium/low) based on completeness of traces.
Trade-offs and choices:
- Chose streaming-first design to support near-real-time dashboards. This increases operational complexity vs. batch-only but reduces time-to-detect regressions.
- Store per-request detail in short-lived hotstore (7d) and aggregate into long-term column store to balance query cost.
- To keep storage bounded we downsample large requests by deterministic hashing for non-SLA customers.
Data contracts and schema: column names and types are documented in Confluence (link below). Use stable versioning and backward-compatible additions.
work_log: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting with product and runtime engineering. Agreed on core fields for decoder output and confidence model.
2026-02-25: Initial schema v0.1 drafted and shared to #console-econ. Outline for KV-marker format added to runtime proto spec.
2026-03-02: Proof-of-concept Flink job implemented to join traces with model-profile table; validated on 3h production trace sample. Observed ~3.8% variance vs billing rollups for one model family.
2026-03-08: Design review with security: flagged PII risk in customer lookup flow, agreed to perform lookups inside VPC-only enrichment step. Security action tracked.
2026-03-12: Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/realtime-econ/pull/267 with initial decoder logic; awaiting review from infra and runtime.
2026-03-14: Integrated fallback heuristic for broken traces; added low-confidence tagging and emitted summary metrics to staging dashboard.
comments: PM review (Jordan Patel) 2026-02-22: Please ensure decoder emits version metadata so downstream can backfill if schema changes.
Design feedback (Sasha R.) 2026-03-03: Prefer confidence buckets (high/med/low) rather than continuous score for easier dashboarding.
Infra note (Priya S.) 2026-03-09: Flink job needs autoscaling knobs and backfill capability; recommend adding watermark+replay window config.
Security (Amir K.) 2026-03-10: Move customer_id enrichment into a private VPC worker; do not log raw customer identifiers in staging logs.
